findings.failure_scenario: If the landed promotion/classification change broke an importer (a circular import or a call-site signature mismatch in another test module importing reckon.crew.promotion), nothing in the recorded evidence would show it: the two-file head arm never imports those modules through the importer population, and no completed importer arm exists to compare.
findings.summary: The done_when requires the test files importing the two changed modules to add no failure against a base arm, run with pytest -n 8; the importer arms never reached a summary (base capped twice, head stopped under the two-failure rule) and the recorded gate ran two files without -n 8, yet the manifest records status complete with rubric.goal_fidelity and rubric.evidence both reading 'missing'.

findings.failure_scenario: A high-volume caller that classifies many settled pointers with a moving worktree head pays a git read per pointer; the mitigation is the cache, and where the cache is cold the settled path now does work the previous design reserved for dead-run adjudication.
findings.summary: classify_pointer now calls _commits_beyond_base(record) for every terminal-status pointer, where the removed comment stated live and settled delivery paths deliberately never paid a git read; the cost is mitigated by the revision-keyed cache in recovery_watch._commits_beyond_base but the deliberate previous choice is reversed without a note.

findings.failure_scenario: A run whose manifest cites a commit landed on a different branch or an amended history drops that citation without a warning, so promotion presents fewer commits than the manifest declared while the record gives no signal that a citation was discarded.
findings.summary: _promotion_commits returns the git history range whenever it is non-empty, so a manifest citation naming a commit outside base..HEAD is silently discarded rather than merged or reported, and the docstring describes the manifest as fallback only.
